scenes.sub: Java sends a SELECT to the database.
The rows come back as a ResultSet, like a small table.
Think of a finger 👉 above the first row.
Returns true if there is a row, false at the end.
Read columns by name or number (1-based).
Repeat for every row, then close.

mnemonics.label: Points trick
mnemonics.html: Before First, Next is True = Cursor starts before first row; next() returns true while rows remain

code.title: Program: read all items
lines: ResultSet rs = st.executeQuery("SELECT ItemID, Name, UnitPrice FROM Item");

steps.say: Run SELECT → get ResultSet. Cursor is before row 1.
Read the 3 columns (by name or index 3).
Loop again for row 2, 3… then next() gives false and the loop stops.

answer_html:
Definition

Query execution means sending a SELECT statement with executeQuery() and reading the returned ResultSet row by row.

Key points

  • ResultSet rs = st.executeQuery(sql);
  • The cursor starts before the first row.
  • rs.next() moves to the next row; returns false at the end.
  • Read values with getInt(), getString(), getDouble(), getDate() by column name or number (starts at 1).
  • Close ResultSet, Statement and Connection after use.
